name: Austere Systems Limited
sector: Software development and IT-enabled project services
summary: Evidence-complete conditional review, not an investment endorsement. Revenue and operating earnings grew, but poor restated cash conversion, older receivables, historical financial-presentation differences and a confirmed competition case require a financial-reliability hold. A claim-funded parent-only diagnostic returns 16.61% in the base case at the observed ₹43 quote; IAS remains NS under G2. IPO deposits are ring-fenced rather than counted twice as surplus cash.

score_note: Thirteen explicit factors, no renormalization. BQS/GQS are non-ranking diagnostics because G2 is held; GQS capped5 for persistent cash conversion weakness, IAS NS regardless of computed raw diagnostic. Forecast reliability is not upgraded by mechanical model precision.

gates.reason: A confirmed historical competition finding and appellate dismissal warrant a governance discount. Specific remediation and final appeal outcome remain unresolved. No automatic current severe-governance failure is inferred solely from the monetary penalty; no recurrence or diversion is established.

IPO restatement explains much of the profit difference and overall cash balances reconcile, but original/restated operating-versus-financing cash categorization, FY26 continuity and benefit disclosures remain materially unresolved for an investable valuation. Bounded source-specific factors are still shown; all numerical rankings are withheld.

Restrained no-rescue survival uses a 20% sales decline, 12% operating margin, quarter-loss of older receivables, extra collection delay and full modeled company claims. Minimum unrestricted cash remains ₹1.4534 crore while earmarks stay restricted. The remote combined stress fails but does not alone establish actual distress or justify G3 Fail.

49 of 60 reference sessions observed; absence is not automatically no-trade. Lot 2,000 shares and coarse historical liquidity are restrictive. No verified current BSE depth, spread, circuit queue or surveillance clearance; an NSE security-master status code is not a BSE suspension determination.

financial_history.basis: Original annual-report comparative, kept separate from IPO-restated series. The reported CFO category is not treated as economically comparable across the two publications.

sections.title: 1. Executive Verdict
sections.text: Austere is a small project-led technology supplier, not a proven recurring software compounder. FY26 revenue was ₹22.2887 crore and reported PAT ₹5.0394 crore, but a large deposit pool and nonoperating income make headline P/E misleading. The base funded diagnostic produces 16.61% over five years at the secondary October19 close of ₹43. That does not remove G2: IAS is NS and the company is excluded from numerical quality rankings until the financial-presentation issues are reconciled. BQS 4.68 and GQS 5.00 are explicitly diagnostic, not endorsement. [S1,S4,M1]

sections.title: 2. Research Header, Gates and Data Confidence
sections.text: Scope is the FY26 standalone parent, with separate IPO-restated FY23–25 history and disclosed post-year entities. Cutoff is October20,2026, with October19 the last reference market session. G1 Conditional, G2 Hold, G3 Conditional and G4 Conditional are distinct decisions. Annual disclosures are High confidence as reported; historical economic comparability is Medium/limited, future forecasts Low, and a verified current bid/ask is absent. New entities are not silently consolidated at100% or assigned revenue without statements. [S1,S4,M1]

sections.title: 3. Scorecard and Calculation Audit
sections.text: Canonical factors are GOV4, MOAT4, REV6, DUR5, CAP5, CASH3, BAL7, EXEC5, EARN4, R6, D4, P3 and L1. Exact BQS is 4.68; raw GQS 5.05 is capped at5 for persistent weak cash realization. Raw IAS 4.470 is not an investable score: G2 forces final IAS NS. All primitive scores are Medium input confidence; none claims a five-year/full-cycle9–10 history. No missing-value renormalization or neutral substitutions are used. The ₹5 lakh reference is illustrative, not the user’s proposed allocation.

sections.title: 4. Business Overview
sections.text: The company supplies software development, IT-enabled services, enterprise applications, digital-transformation projects, analytics and AI services, and in-house products. Economics depend on delivery staff, project acceptance, collection timing and customer retention. FY26 employment was154. The annual report identifies154 employees and operations in Pune/Gurugram with a Panchkula office, but revenue is not sufficiently segmented to infer recurring subscription economics or geography-specific margins. Government and corporate project exposures require separate bid, delivery and collection judgments. [S1,S4]

sections.title: 5. Moat / Industry Position
sections.text: RHP FY25 mix was71.67% analytics/AI and28.33% in-house products, versus64.61%/35.33% a year earlier; these are revenue labels, not evidence of subscription renewal or proprietary network effects. FY25 domestic revenue was85.05%. FY26 disclosed exports fell to ₹2.3262 crore from ₹2.7831 crore, supporting caution about an export-growth narrative. Peer names in the RHP, including ASM Technologies, MosChip, InfoBeans, Onward and3iInfotech, differ in engineering/product mix, scale and accounting perimeter. Their multiples are contextual and are not imported into valuation. The chosen6×/8×/11× exit EBIT range is an analyst stress range, not a quoted peer median. [S1,S4]

sections.title: 6. Revenue Growth & Scale
sections.text: RHP revenue of ₹15.3588/18.5657/18.6205 crore for FY23/FY24/FY25 and FY26 revenue ₹22.2887 crore yield about13.22% three-year growth. FY25 growth was only0.30%, followed by19.70% inFY26. REV6 follows the10–15% band without an uplift. Reported original-basis PAT grew76.3% from ₹2.8586 crore, while the prior IPO-restated PAT was ₹4.0133 crore. A25.6% comparison to that alternative denominator is informative but not a verified same-policy growth rate. Restated and original histories remain separately labeled; weighted-average EPS is not used as the current share count. [S1,S4]

sections.title: 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.text: Operating EBIT excluding other income rose from ₹3.7223 crore to ₹5.7777 crore on the annual comparative basis. A25.17%-tax incremental NOPAT/IC diagnostic gives roughly7.14% including noncurrent FDs and38.62% excluding them, against an assumed12–16% capital-cost range. That spread reflects idle IPO capital and denominator sensitivity, not proven project ROIC. FY26 cash capex was ₹1.7695 crore; other long advances consumed another ₹1.4295 crore. March31 unused IPO proceeds were ₹13.8246 crore: ₹11.6 crore for working capital and ₹2.2246 crore remaining general-corporate allocation. The model funds positive incremental WC and eligible capex from their respective pools, not unrelated dividends or legal claims. New commitments include ₹0.0051 crore for51% of Austere Next and ₹0.02 crore for Neural Nexis AI LLP; the wholly owned Delaware LLC had no initial capital contribution. No unverified group earnings are assigned. [S1]

sections.title: 8. Management, Governance & Execution
sections.text: The CCI’s April 4, 2022 order imposed a ₹44,25,569 company penalty for bid coordination in historical soil-testing tenders. The NCLAT dismissed the company’s appeal on September 23, 2025, as reported in the CCI’s official appellate bulletin. Austere disputes the finding and penalty methodology and states that it appealed to the Supreme Court. Official Supreme Court lists independently identify CA 79/2026 and a January 5, 2026 procedural direction to list it with CA 7883/2024; the accessible list is not a final judgment or proof of a stay. No final Supreme Court disposition was established through the research cutoff. An October 2, 2026 exchange-filings index identifies a SEBI warning-cum-advisory disclosure and a separate NCLAT disclosure. The original linked PDFs were inaccessible, so the warning’s exact terms and the company’s detailed response are not independently verified here; it is not treated as a new quantified penalty or proof of a new substantive competition violation. Related-party lending of ₹0.1595 crore to FIMO is distinct from ₹1.4295 crore advances to others; the latter is not automatically classified as related-party. The director-remuneration aggregate in note60 and individual amounts in note34 require an accrual/payment reconciliation before concluding impropriety. Governance4 reflects documented concerns with offsets, not a claim of current fraud or a mandatory severe override. [S1,S2,S3,S5,S6,S7,S8]

sections.title: 9. Financial Forensics
sections.text: FY25 operating cash flow is ₹3.8445 crore in the subsequent annual comparative versus ₹0.51114 crore in the IPO-restated statement. Total annual cash movement reconciles to approximately ₹4.0124 crore on both presentations, so this is not a finding of missing cash. The category differences are approximately +₹3.33336 crore operating, −₹0.35319 crore investing and −₹2.98013 crore financing in the annual comparative relative to the RHP. The RHP includes ₹3.25994 crore equity proceeds, while the annual comparative identifies only ₹0.6381 crore share proceeds and reports ₹1.9178 crore other operating adjustments. A full economic line-item reconciliation was not provided in the accessible disclosures; the FY26 continuation of those historical classifications remains an analytical limitation. Restated FY23–25 cumulative CFO/PAT is about0.325; FY26 original CFO/PAT is about0.696 and after cash capex leaves ₹1.7399 crore before other investment. These are separately labeled diagnostics. Receivables were ₹10.4967 crore, including ₹3.6253 crore over six months and ₹0.3677 crore classified doubtful over three years; the book does not clearly reconcile allowance coverage. The FY26 benefit table shows gratuity ₹0.5341 crore, while the current and noncurrent balance-sheet notes total ₹0.3541 crore. The model reserves the ₹0.18 crore difference rather than treating either figure as definitively correct. This is a disclosed presentation inconsistency, not an allegation of misappropriation. Gross current tax ₹1.7832 crore and TDS/TCS credit ₹1.9313 crore are modeled separately, while the ₹0.0741 crore wrong-TAN recovery is not counted as cash. All tax, statutory, employee, dividend, interest and contingent claims have a unique treatment. [S1,S4]

sections.title: 10. Valuation & Market Expectations
sections.text: The model starts with actual March31 balances and has67 dated monthly cash rows through October2031, with the first seven months an estimate rather than actual September/October balances. Bear/base/bull revenue growth is2%/10%/18%, operating margin16%/22%/26%, and exit EBIT multiple6×/8×/11×. Resulting funded terminal prices are ₹44.00/₹92.70/₹190.41; annualized diagnostics are 0.46%/16.61%/34.66%. No future FD interest or rental income is capitalized into operating earnings. Only free non-IPO long FD ₹3.8842 crore is carried at face value to exit, and unspent IPO earmarks are excluded. Opening accrued interest is recovered once; long advances, security assets and DTA have no automatic terminal value. All company litigation claims are conservatively paid over12months, not asserted actually due. The September-record-date ₹0.80 dividend is deducted from corporate cash but not paid to the October entrant. The15% hurdle corresponds to a conditional entry ₹46.09 or about8.17% growth with other base assumptions unchanged. These are parent-only scenarios under G2 Hold, not fair-value targets. [S1,S4,M1]

sections.title: 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.text: Credible restrained survival combines20% lower sales,12% operating margin,25% loss on the disclosed older-receivable pool, ₹0.5 crore additional collection delay, full modeled company legal claims and legacy-benefit settlement. It remains funded without debt or rescue, with minimum cash ₹1.4534 crore. The impairment reduces opening recoverable WC and is added back once as noncash, then replacement WC is funded once. The extreme boundary stacks45% lower sales,3% margin, loss of all older receivables, ₹3 crore delay, tax-credit deferral and locked short FDs; it becomes unfunded in June2026, an estimated stub date, and has no investor IRR. This is not an actual default finding or the basis for G3 Fail. A separate hypothetical debt/equity rescue includes12% interest,3% equity fees and half-price dilution; it does not demonstrate that rescue exists. Permanent loss can arise from project-margin collapse, uncollectible claims, legal/tender consequences or destructive capital deployment despite current cash. [S1]

sections.title: 12. 5× / 10× Feasibility
sections.text: With no multiple change or dilution,5× and10× in five years require about37.97% and58.49% annual per-share value growth. The base operating growth assumption is10%, verified revenue CAGR about13.2%, and bull18%, so a spectacular outcome needs unusually strong growth and/or rerating beyond the ordinary case. FY26 full-issued-share PAT per share is about₹4.81, below reported weighted-average EPS₹5.47; IPO dilution matters. No unproven AI narrative, large-TAM label or new subsidiary grants a separate multibagger premium. The model does not make5×/10× a likely forecast. [S1,S4]

sections.title: 13. Monitoring Plan
sections.text: Before reassessment, request a line-by-line original/restated cash-flow bridge and consistent FY26 comparative, reconciled employee-benefit and remuneration disclosures, current IPO-use balances, collections/allowance coverage of older receivables, and post-year consolidated ownership/cash commitments. Check the actual Supreme Court order and any stay or final disposition, rather than relying on cause-list appearance. Obtain the original October2 disclosures and evidence of specific compliance remediation. Reassess after the next signed half-year/annual results, or sooner upon a material legal, capital or ownership change. Execution requires current BSE lot, restrictions, depth and spread verification. These are analytical triggers, not a promise of automated monitoring. [S1,S5,S6,M1]

sections.title: 14. Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.text: Final classification is financial-reliability watchlist, not compounder or favorable investment candidate. The accessible-evidence review and funded diagnostic are complete, but G2 blocks IAS and all numerical quality rankings. High cash and nil borrowings are genuine offsets to funding risk; they do not resolve presentation consistency or collection quality. Do not substitute an attractive conditional16.61% model return for documentary reliability. A future upgrade would require the specified reconciliations, cash realization, disciplined proceeds deployment and sufficient market execution evidence. [S1,S4,M1]

sections.title: 15. Sources, Assumptions & Open Questions
sections.text: Primary annual-report pages, the historical CCI order, official CCI appellate reporting and Supreme Court procedural listings anchor the findings. The issuer-authored RHP was inspected through an indexed third-party mirror after original sources failed; its local download was not a valid PDF and the page-image request failed. Current price/liquidity and the October2 filing discovery are secondary. Sources distinguish reviewed text from inaccessible PDFs. Annual figures use lakh while the RHP uses hundreds; all calculations here convert to crore. Source dates, restrictions, original/restated bases, estimated stub, model assumptions, exact score arithmetic and opening-claim treatments remain explicit. No missing source is silently treated as cleared or zero. [S1,S2,S3,S4,S5,S6,M1]

ranking_eligibility.reason: G2 financial reliability hold excludes numerical rankings. Completed analysis does not mean investable or all source gaps resolved.

valuation.method: 67 dated monthly rows; first seven months estimated. Parent-only operating diagnostic with no new subsidiary earnings or value; 51% subsidiary and unknown LLP economics not misrepresented as wholly owned group forecasts. All actual opening claims classified once. Earmarked WC and GCP deposits fund eligible modeled uses only; unspent balances excluded from distributable terminal value. Non-IPO long FD carried at face value only at exit, with no future yield. Gross opening tax paid and credits recovered separately; wrong-TAN recoverable excluded. Nonoperating advances, rental deposit asset and DTA excluded unless explicit recovery sensitivity. Reported contingent claims are paid conservatively over 12 months, not asserted due or forecast legal outcome. Larger of conflicting employee-benefit disclosures reserved; old and September-record-date dividends deducted with no entitlement to the October entrant. Future maintenance and replacement working capital funded; impairment reduces recoverable opening WC once with equal noncash addback. No ordinary debt or rescue assumed. No investor IRR on unfunded paths. G2 reliability hold prevents interpreting diagnostic returns as investable IAS or recommendation.

GOV.reason: Historical competition finding and continuing appeal are documented; disclosure of the claim and liquidity are offsets, while specific remediation remains unproved. No automatic severe override.

MOAT.reason: IT project and in-house product capability is real, but retention, pricing power and contractual recurring revenue are not demonstrated. Analytics/AI labels are not proof of a SaaS moat.

REV.reason: FY23–26 revenue CAGR about 13.2% maps to the 10–15% band; FY25 was nearly flat, so no uplift. Three-year evidence does not merit a high-confidence full-cycle score.

DUR.reason: Domestic digital projects and product cross-selling provide runway; concentration, tender eligibility and contract renewal economics remain uncertain.

CAP.reason: IPO FD classification drives incremental return diagnostics from roughly 7% to 39%; deployment and project economics are not yet proven. Score reflects mixed rather than assumed outstanding reinvestment.

CASH.reason: FY23–25 restated cumulative CFO/PAT is about 0.325, with weak conversion across the period and worsening receivable ageing into FY26. This is scored from the restated series and ageing, not by splicing the original comparative CFO. Persistent conversion weakness triggers GQS cap5.

BAL.reason: No reported debt and meaningful cash/FDs cover restrained stress. Earmarked proceeds, aged assets, contingent claims and deposit accessibility prevent a stronger score.

EXEC.reason: FY26 sales and operating EBIT improved, but receivable ageing, idle IPO capital and reporting inconsistencies limit demonstrated execution quality.

EARN.reason: Restated PAT rose sharply then declined slightly in FY25, and FY26 comparisons are affected by original/restated bases, nonoperating income and IPO dilution. Operating improvement is visible but normalized per-share persistence is not established.

R.reason: Conditional funded base diagnostic IRR16.61% maps to17%-below band score6 at a15% hurdle; not a recommendation, with IAS independently held by G2.

D.reason: Bear diagnostic is roughly flat over five years, yet unreliable historical classification, tender issues and collection risk can impair capital. Cash-backed restrained survival is an offset, not downside certainty.

P.reason: The model has conservative claim reserves and survives restrained stress, but reporting and contract-quality uncertainty makes a favorable durable outcome low-confidence as a forecast. Input assumptions are explicit and reproducible.

L.reason: Observed-only ₹5 lakh exit estimate29.41days at5% already exceeds20days; 2,000-share lots and unverified missing dates/depth add friction.

liquidity.limitations: Low×volume is a lower-bound proxy, not observed turnover. Missing dates have unknown coverage/trading status and are not filled with zero. Actual exit can be slower; no depth/spread/queue guarantee. This is an illustrative position, not a recommendation.
